task_1.title: Restore PyPI license metadata for attrs releases
task_1.description: The upgrade addresses incorrect or missing PyPI license metadata so package consumers and registries can see the library's licensing information again. The provided evidence does not indicate any runtime, API, or behavioral change beyond distribution metadata correctness.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading from 24.3.0 to 25.1.0 restores correct license metadata in the published package metadata so PyPI and downstream consumers can recognize the project's license information.

expectation.grounded: Published distribution metadata for the library should once again expose license information correctly on PyPI. Based on the provided release note and the absence of any code diff, no public runtime API additions, removals, or behavior changes are evidenced for this upgrade.
expectation.conceptual: After the upgrade, users and tooling that inspect package metadata should be able to see the project's license information correctly. Application behavior when importing or using the library should remain unchanged.

constraints.grounded: Do not introduce new runtime semantics, public API changes, or behavior changes that are not supported by the release note. Treat this upgrade as a packaging metadata correction only, because the provided code diff shows no observable runtime change.
constraints.conceptual: The change should be limited to making package metadata accurate and should not alter how the library behaves in normal use.

behavior: Package metadata published for the upgraded release includes recognizable license information for PyPI consumers.
The upgrade does not evidence any change to import behavior, callable behavior, warnings, exceptions, or return values.
The primary observable effect is in package index and metadata inspection workflows rather than application runtime behavior.
acceptance_criteria: When consumers inspect the upgraded package metadata on PyPI or through standard packaging metadata tools, the project's license information should be present and recognizable.
When applications upgrade from 24.3.0 to 25.1.0 and use the library through its existing public APIs, they should observe no behavioral change attributable to this release.
The upgrade should resolve the metadata regression where license information was missing or not recognized in 24.3.0.
